newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW - SALE eyes Asian aircraft leasing market.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - SALE eyes Asian aircraft leasing market.

text.p: Singapore Aircraft Leasing Enterprise (SALE), a unit of Singapore Airlines, is plans to expand in Asia when it takes delivery of 12 new aircaft over the next two years, managing director said on Monday.
John Willingham told Reuters in an interview that SALE would take delivery of six A320 aircraft from Airbus in 1998 and another six in 1999.
SALE also has on option another 12 A320s, some of which will be exercised towards the end of this year, he said.
The company has also ordered 16 Boeing B777 -- six firm orders and 10 on option. The first two will be delivered in 1999.

The leasing company, jointly owned by SIA and U.S.-based Boullioun Aviation Services Inc which is in turn a subsidiary of Sumitomo Trust and Banking Company Ltd's, plans to have at least 40 aircraft by 2001.

"From our base in Singapore, we will have a strong focus on the Asian market. The Chinese market will be an important one for us, certainly for the A320s and maybe down the line, also the B777s," he said.
Willingham said SALE was likely to announce commitments for some of its A320s "in the next couple of months".
Other Asian markets with good potential for aircraft leasing include South Korea, Taiwan, Indonesia, Vietnam and Australia. Opportunities are also opening up in Malaysia and Thailand, he said.
The Asian aviation market is growing strongly and fleet growth is increasing by about seven to eight percent a year compared with three to four percent in Europe and the United States.
SALE's growth was expected to pick up sharply in 1998 and 1999 when it takes delivery of its new aircraft, Willingham said.
Combined with Boullioun's 26 aircraft, SALE, which now has six, should be a major operator in the global aircraft leasing market by the year 2001, he added.
"By that time, we should be in the number three position," Willingham said.
The two dominant operators now are American International Group's International Lease Finance Corp (ILFC) and General Electric Company's GECAS.
Willingham also said SALE would have to look into drawing in fresh capital as it expands its fleet.
SIA and Boullioun each put in US$250 million to establish SALE in 1993 and about $100 million of the capital has been invested so far.
Willingham said SALE has enough capital to fund all the aircraft it had committed to buy, but not for the aircraft on option.
He said the company could raise more money from its existing shareholders or draw in fresh funds from large private investors. Over the medium term, the company could consider a public listing.
